traps.evidence: "Brassica → Corn Exchange → Fjaerland (Norway) → Saltmarsh" — named with no role, lab, or research claim attached.
"Animated counter for the 14kg→5kg waste reduction." — used unscoped as a live personal headline stat.
Timeline listed employers with no dates at all; neither March 2022 nor September 2022 appears in the first reply.
"3D page-turn/flipbook through the four issues"; "The 60 restaurant photos, your larder phone photos, the Brine scans ... aren't in the folder." No credit or permission raised.

final.question: the site moves like a walk through her kitchen, from raw trim to finished ferment, matching her own framing that most of the work happens before service

swap.reason: The spine is her particular material — the jar wall, the koji cupboard, the 40+ ferments and the ferment log — not generic chef-portfolio furniture.

backdrop.reason: The plan's own fallback is "static imagery swapped in for WebGL", conceding the jar wall, shelf grid and flipbook carry no information a picture or list could not.

depth.reason: Despite the "trim to finished ferment" claim, the running order is a conventional section stack — Ask Ines, Brine, Apprentices, Recommendation could be reshuffled with nothing lost.

clipart.reason: There is no single central object: a hero jar wall, a separate evolving jar, a shelf grid and a flipbook are four unrelated 3D scenes.

honesty.reason: The final plan scopes the waste figure to prep and plate over one month in 2023, dates the title to September 2022, and calls Fjaerland a ten-week unpaid stage.

thirty_seconds.reason: The hero gives name, title and a line of philosophy, but proof and contact sit in sections 8 and 9 with no nav or header route to them.

plain_reader.reason: The planned opening is her own plain framing — trim, whey, stems, bones — which reads clearly to an outsider and credibly to a cook.

judgement.summary: This is a single-concept plan, "The Larder", that walks the visitor from raw trim to finished ferment across nine fairly conventional sections, decorated with four separate WebGL set pieces and anchored on her real ferment log; after the corrections it states her history and the waste figure honestly and flags its own placeholders. Its greatest weakness is that the 3D is scenery rather than structure — no one object persists, the section order is interchangeable, and the practical layer (phone layout, typefaces, how a visitor reaches her in the first thirty seconds) is largely unaddressed.
